analysis:
This PR is a dependency bump only. desktop-app/package.json (lines 32, 39) moves electron 44.5.1 to 44.9.1 and vite 8.3.2 to 8.3.5 (dev dependencies). desktop-app/package-lock.json is updated to match: the vite/rolldown/oxc transitive chain, and the head tail (6239-7040) shows vite 8.3.5 and unchanged registry.npmjs.org resolved URLs with sha512 integrity fields. landing/package-lock.json moves next 16.2.6 to 16.4.1, sharp platform packages 0.34.5 to 0.35.5, libvips 1.2.4 to 1.3.4, @swc/helpers, and adds wasm32 and freebsd sharp packages plus bundled @emnapi entries for tailwind's wasm32-wasi. All new entries use the official npm registry with integrity hashes, and no git URLs, tarball hosts or install scripts were introduced in the visible text.

No provider-process, coordinator WebSocket, attestation, App Attest, cache or fan-helper code is touched, so TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011 and TB-012 and the threats under them are unaffected by the diff. The changes sit in the out-of-scope console and landing areas, or in the desktop frontend's build and package tooling. Electron is a patch-level security-oriented bump within major 44, which does not weaken the supply-chain posture. Limits on coverage: the patch excerpts for the lock files are truncated, so I could not check every changed lockfile entry, and I did not independently verify the integrity hashes against the registry. Whether desktop-app interacts with the provider's trust boundaries (e.g. signing or packaging of the official build for T-054) cannot be judged from these units. Nothing here suggests a regression, so I report no findings. The lockfile partial coverage is a minor residual uncertainty, not a material one.
